Explaining Your Ideas

When working on a math problem, it is important to show how you solved the problem and explain your thinking. Adding text can help, but showing connections with arrows between mathematical objects to explain the connection can be a huge help.

We will be looking at:

  1. Sparrows
  2. Sharing workspaces
  3. Files

highlightedText.text: To finish the What If... you will explore all three using the instructions below.

text:
1. Sparrows

Sparrows allow you to connect mathematical objects and describe how they relate. They come in two forms.

  • Curved Sparrows
  • Straight Sparrows

When you select the sparrow button at the top of your workspace all tiles that accept sparrows become outlined in blue.

Note: You can only add, delete, and edit sparrows when you have the sparrow button selected. You cannot edit tiles when the sparrow button is selected.

Copy the table and graph below into your workspace under the What If...? heading. Notice the straight sparrow isn't pointing to the same place. Let's fix it while looking at the difference between curved and straight sparrows.

  1. Click on each end of both sparrows and notice you are only able to move one and the rest are anchored to points on the graph or cells in the table. Note: Straight sparrows require one end to be anchored while curved sparrows require both ends to be anchored
  2. Delete the straight sparrow by clicking on the 'x' that appears when you hover over the line
  3. Create a new curved sparrow that starts at the highest point on the graph and connects to the number 16 in the table.
  4. Type '4*4=16' or describe the relationship in another way using text
  5. Move the text so that it doesn't get in the way of anything else on your workspace
  6. Hide all your sparrows

2. Sharing Workspaces

CLUE is designed so that you can learn with others in your group and in your class. Discussing and sharing your work is an important part of the learning process.

Sharing your work with your group is controlled with the button and slider switch in the upper right corner of your workspace. The button on the left toggles your workspace view from your individual view to a group view. In the group view, your work is always in the upper left corner. You can see the initials of your group members in each window pane.

The Share slider makes your work visible to your group members and to your class.

Your group members cannot change your work and you can’t change theirs. However, you can drag tiles from your group members’ workspaces and they can drag tiles from your workspace. You will see soon how to view and borrow from class members outside your group.

Switch to group view and turn on sharing. Ask your group members to do the same. Look at your group members’ work in the Initial Challenge. Find your favorite image or sketch from someone else's work.

You can zoom into each window by placing your cursor at the center of the four windows, and dragging the window panes to see more detail.

  1. Copy your favorite image or sketch into your workspace by dragging the tile and placing it under the What If...? heading.
  2. Now edit it and expand on it. Your group member can even bring your edited version over into their What If...?!

Think about how useful this could be while doing math! Imagine that you’re working on a problem, and your group member finds a different way to solve it. You can trade your solutions! Or, maybe you're in a disagreement with your group member over a solution. You can both see each others work at the same time and compare!

3. Files

In the upper left corner of your workspace is the File menu. To create new files for your personal use or to edit existing files, use the File dropdown menu. You might create files to try something out or take notes.

Open allows you to create a new document by clicking the New Workspace icon. You can also access documents that are associated with the problem you are working on. The Workspaces tab shows your current problem document on top and any new documents that you may have created below the divider line.

With the Learning Log tab you can create files that you can see and edit throughout the entire Unit. This is a good place to summarize your learning.

The Bookmark tab shows documents that you may have highlighted as important from My Work or Class Work on the My Resources page.

Create a new file and add a sentence about something you're looking forward to.

Sparrows and Explaining Your Ideas

When working on a math problem, it is important to show how you solved the problem and explain your thinking. Adding text can help, but showing connections with arrows between mathematical objects to explain the connection can be a huge help.

Sparrows have many uses. They come in two forms.

  • Curved, two-ended Sparrows
  • Straight, one-ended Sparrows

Sparrows connect mathematical objects. This includes points, lines, shapes on any graphs or cells in a table.

To Use Sparrows

Select the sparrow button at the top of the your workspace. All tiles that accept sparrows become outlined in blue.

Click and release the start point of the sparrow. Move your mouse to the desired connection point and click. Enter text in the small textbox on the mid-point of the sparrow to explain why you have made that connection. When finished, click the sparrow button again or click the selection pointer. To edit, click the sparrow button again. When selected there is an "x" on the sparrow to delete it. You can drag curved sparrows by the text box to move the curve.

Two examples of sparrow use below. Create your own sparrows! You can drag these tiles into your workspace or go back to the tables and number lines in the Initial Challenge tab if you wish!

Sharing Work in Your Group

CLUE is designed so that you can learn with others in your group and in your class. Discussing and sharing your work is an important part of the learning process.

Sharing your work with your group is controlled with the button and slider switch in the upper right corner of your workspace. The button on the left toggles your workspace view from your individual view to a group view. In the group view, your work is always in the upper left corner. You can see the initials of your group members in each window pane.

Once students get started with the mathematical activities, feel free to direct them in the use of sharing. Some teachers prefer students to work independently initially, and have students share their work with their group after their first attempts at problem-solving. For each student, sharing to the group is off by default, but it is controlled by the student. However, students who have trouble getting started often get a lift from their peers by seeing how others are tackling the problems. Think of group sharing as a tool that you can use flexibly by directing your students according to their needs.

The Share slider makes your work visible to your group members and to your class.

Your group members cannot change your work and you can’t change theirs. However, you can drag tiles from your group members’ workspaces and they can drag tiles from your workspace. You will see soon how to view and borrow from class members outside your group.

Switch to group view and turn on sharing. Ask your group members to do the same. You can zoom into each window by placing your cursor at the center of the four windows, and dragging the window panes to see more detail.

Look at your group members’ work in the Introduction. Did they write a haiku? In the Initial Challenge did they do something fun with the dog graph?

If you like something from your group members’ work, copy it by dragging your neighbor’s tile and placing it in your What if...? Section, for example. Then you can edit it and expand on it. Your neighbor may want to copy it back after your changes.

Why is this useful when doing math? Imagine that you’re working on a problem and your neighbor finds a different way to solve it. You can trade your solutions. Or, maybe you are stuck on how to start a problem. Perhaps your neighbors can help you get going.

Create or Edit Files

In the upper left corner of your workspace is the File menu. To create new files for your personal use or to edit existing files, use the File dropdown menu. You might create files to try something out or take notes. Below are the things you can do. Try them out.

With the Learning Log tab you can create files that you can see and edit throughout the entire Unit. This is a good place to summarize your learning.

The Bookmark tab shows documents that you may have highlighted as important from My Work or Class Work on the My Resources page.

Make a copy copies your present workspace. This copy is not shared automatically with your group. Give it a new name. It is your private copy, although you can share it if you wish.
